deliverables: Open, standardized interface across Cardano on-chain protocols
Documentation, auto-generated SDKs in multiple languages, and live JSON-RPC endpoints from verified interface definitions
Agent-first documentation, protocol skills packaging operations, and an MCP server for agents to discover and call published protocols
Onboarding of 12 additional protocols over 12 months, 3 per quarter, with developer and agent coverage
Milestone-based disbursement controls and reporting obligations through Intersect oversight
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, submitted by Intersect on behalf of the vendor TxPipe
request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Tx3 by TxPipe, described as an open API layer for Cardano dApp protocols with developer and AI-agent-facing infrastructure.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,308,000 ADA plus a 327,000 ADA contingency reserve over 12 months, with a total withdrawal of 1,684,050 ADA including a 49,050 ADA Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Tx3 is intended to provide a standard open-source interface to Cardano protocols, including documentation, multi-language SDKs, and live RPC endpoints.
The proposal claims Cardano currently lacks a common interface mechanism across ecosystem protocols, forcing integrators to relearn each protocol and rebuild understanding independently.
TxPipe has already put the developer layer into production through Catalyst Fund 14 with 5 protocols live on the Tx3 Protocol Registry at https://tx3.land.
The proposal funds 12 additional protocol onboardings, at 3 per quarter, plus development of an MCP server and skill framework as shared infrastructure for registry protocols.
The proposal states that protocols including Strike Finance, Indigo Protocol, VyFinance, Bodega Market, and Fluid Tokens are already accessible through Tx3.

The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission under the approved process.
The requested amount is claimed not to breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit at submission, either alone or in aggregate, for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.

TxPipe is said to have received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule, plus 2025 Intersect open-source maintenance funding for Pallas, Dolos, and UTxO RPC that is on schedule.

Intersect states that funds will be managed through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multi-party authorization thresholds, an Oversight Committee, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.

summary: The document asks for 1,684,050 ADA to fund TxPipe's Tx3 over 12 months, expanding a protocol interface registry and adding AI-agent infrastructure, with Intersect-administered smart-contract custody and oversight.
